bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in json_tokener where a utf8_replacement_char is unnecessarily added if input runs out in the middle of a unicode escape within the json_tokener_state_escape_unicode case, potentially leading to incorrect handling of incomplete unicode sequences.
bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable json-c revision `50179fb09f5d317e7192c781ca4a6b039d7818ae`, `tokener_parse_ex_fuzzer` passes the exact 11-byte witness `"'\\udBdd \\ud"` directly to `json_tokener_parse_ex(tok, data1, size)`. Because the default tokener is non-strict, the leading single quote is accepted and the parser enters `json_tokener_state_escape_unicode` for the first `\u`. The digits `dBdd` decode to high surrogate `0xDBDD`, line 697 stores that value in `tok->got_hi_surrogate`, and because the next byte is a literal space rather than another `\u`, the parser appends `utf8_replacement_char` to `tok->pb` but leaves `tok->got_hi_surrogate` set. The later second escape starts `\ud` and reaches EOF after one hex digit. The vulnerable EOF cleanup at lines 796-800 runs even though `tok->st_pos < 4`, sees stale `tok->got_hi_surrogate`, and calls `strcmp(tok->pb->buf, (char *)utf8_replacement_char)`. `utf8_replacement_char` is a 3-byte global without a trailing NUL, so `strcmp` reads one byte past it and AddressSanitizer reports the saved `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4`. The fix rewrites `json_tokener_state_escape_unicode` so incomplete `\uNNNN` input returns without entering this cleanup comparison.

source.description: The first `\u` in the witness is accepted by the string-escape handler and initializes unicode-escape decode state. This is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that turns attacker-controlled bytes into the parser state later used by the stale-surrogate cleanup.
source.value_from: The exact 11-byte `poc` is `"'\\udBdd \\ud"`. After the leading single quote and backslash are consumed in string parsing, the first attacker-controlled `u` reaches this case and enters `json_tokener_state_escape_unicode`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. During EOF cleanup for the second, incomplete `\ud`, the parser compares the accumulated print buffer against `utf8_replacement_char` with `strcmp`. Because `utf8_replacement_char` is a 3-byte global rather than a NUL-terminated C string, the compare reads past its end.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `strcmp`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `utf8_replacement_char` defined in `json_tokener.c:119` with size 3.

root_cause.description: Incomplete-escape EOF handling is wrong. After the second `\u` has only one hex digit, this cleanup block runs solely on EOF, not on completion of four hex digits. That reuses stale `tok->got_hi_surrogate` from the earlier standalone high surrogate instead of returning with the partial escape state preserved. The fixed commit adds that missing early-return behavior for `tok->st_pos < 4` and never reaches this cleanup compare on an incomplete `\uNNNN`.
root_cause.note: The relevant patch hunk rewrites `json_tokener_state_escape_unicode` so the `tok->st_pos < 4` path advances, checks `PEEK_CHAR`, and `goto out` immediately on short input, removing this vulnerable fallthrough into the cleanup `strcmp`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first decoded escape `\udBdd` is materialized as pending high-surrogate state here. That attacker-derived value remains set across the later incomplete `\ud` and gates the vulnerable EOF cleanup path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The first escape in the exact witness is `\udBdd`; after step 2 decodes those four hex digits to `0xDBDD`, this assignment stores that value in `tok->got_hi_surrogate`.

parser_admitted.description: The default tokener has `JSON_TOKENER_STRICT` clear, so the witness's leading single quote is accepted by the `'` case and the parser enters string mode instead of rejecting the input. That admission is required for the later `\u` escape handling to run.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first `\u` in the witness enters unicode-escape decoding, zeroing the accumulator and digit count and switching the parser into `json_tokener_state_escape_unicode`.

Across the first escape's four hex digits `dBdd`, repeated execution of this line accumulates the attacker-controlled value into `tok->ucs_char`. After the fourth digit, `tok->ucs_char == 0xDBDD` and `tok->st_pos == 4`.
Because `0xDBDD` satisfies `IS_HIGH_SURROGATE(tok->ucs_char)`, the parser saves it as pending surrogate state in `tok->got_hi_surrogate`.

The witness byte after `\udBdd` is a space, so the immediate-following-surrogate test fails and this else arm appends the 3-byte replacement character to `tok->pb`. That path does not clear `tok->got_hi_surrogate`, so stale high-surrogate state and a print buffer beginning with those same three bytes now coexist.

When the later `\u` of the witness is encountered, the parser starts a new unicode escape by resetting `tok->ucs_char` and `tok->st_pos` to 0. The stale `tok->got_hi_surrogate` from step 3 and the print-buffer contents from step 4 remain live.
The second escape supplies only one hex digit `d` before EOF. After this execution, `tok->st_pos == 1` and `tok->ucs_char == 0xD000`, so three hex digits are still missing from the current `\uNNNN`.

Root cause. Advancing past that lone `d` hits EOF, and the vulnerable code immediately enters this cleanup block even though the current escape is incomplete (`tok->st_pos == 1`). The missing obligation, added by the fix, is to return with the partial `\uNNNN` state intact instead of reusing stale-surrogate cleanup logic.

Sink. Because `tok->got_hi_surrogate` is still nonzero, the cleanup evaluates this compare. `utf8_replacement_char` is the 3-byte global at line 119, not a NUL-terminated C string, so `strcmp` reads a fourth byte past it; ASan reports the saved `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` here.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `utf8_replacement_char` defined here with size 3.

poc.trigger: Running the staged witness under the vulnerable ARVO container invokes `tokener_parse_ex_fuzzer`, which passes the exact 11-byte input `"'\\udBdd \\ud"` to `json_tokener_parse_ex(tok, data1, size)` and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` in `strcmp`.

format.name: json-c non-strict quoted string
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact 11-byte input `"'\\udBdd \\ud"`: a non-strict single-quoted JSON string whose first escape is the complete high surrogate `\udBdd`, whose next byte is a literal space rather than the `\u` required for a surrogate pair, and whose second escape starts with `\u` plus one hex digit `d` before EOF without a closing quote. This exact layout leaves `tok->got_hi_surrogate` set from the first escape and makes the second escape end with `tok->st_pos == 1`, reaching the cleanup `strcmp` on `utf8_replacement_char`. The contract does not claim that neighboring escape spellings or other truncations take the same path.
